gessi.tagline: Italian brassware that treats water as design.
gessi.onDisplay: Gessi brassware across the bathroom displays, and the Haute Culture collection by private appointment [confirm what is on the floor].

knownFor.title: Private Wellness
knownFor.text: Showers, steam and bathing designed as a system rather than a set of taps — Gessi's own phrase for the spa at home.

knownFor.title: Finishes
knownFor.text: Brushed brass, copper, black metal, warm bronze and more, matched across every piece in a room.

knownFor.title: Haute Culture
knownFor.text: The couture tier: eight collections made by hand, available through ten UK showrooms, of which Zest is one.

knownFor.title: Made in one place
knownFor.text: Designed and manufactured at Parco Gessi in Piedmont, which is why finishes match and spares exist a decade later.

whyZest: Gessi is a specification brand. Which valve, which rough-in, which finish on which wall — these are the decisions that make a Gessi bathroom work, and they are made in the design appointment, not the checkout.

We have specified Gessi for over [X] years across homes and [X] apartments, and we are one of ten UK Haute Culture partner showrooms. If something arrives wrong or a part is needed in five years, you ring us, not a marketplace.

faqs.q: Is Gessi more expensive than other Italian brassware?
faqs.a: It sits at the top of the market alongside AXOR and Dornbracht. The design appointment will show you where the money goes and where it needn't.

faqs.q: Can I match finishes across the bathroom and kitchen?
faqs.a: Yes — Gessi makes kitchen taps in the same finishes, which is one reason we design both rooms together.
Gessi's couture collections — Perle, Jacqueline, Ludovica and five more — handmade and specified rather than sold. Zest is one of ten UK showrooms; see the Haute Culture page.

collections.name: Haute Culture
collections.text: Eight couture collections, by private appointment.

collections.name: Venti20 and Inverso
collections.text: Contemporary brassware in Gessi's full finish range.

collections.name: Private Wellness
collections.text: Rain, cascade and body showers; steam and spa systems.

axor.tagline: Hansgrohe's design house, with the architects' names attached.
axor.onDisplay: AXOR brassware on several displays, including [collections — confirm].

knownFor.title: Designer collections
knownFor.text: Philippe Starck, Antonio Citterio, Barber Osgerby, Jean-Marie Massaud — each collection is a named collaboration.

knownFor.title: FinishPlus
knownFor.text: Fifteen PVD finishes applied in-house, from brushed bronze to polished gold optic, with matching accessories.

knownFor.title: Engineering
knownFor.text: Hansgrohe's valves and thermostats underneath, which is why it works as well as it looks.

knownFor.title: Signature
knownFor.text: A made-to-order service for one-off finishes and configurations.

whyZest: AXOR is sold widely online, often at a discount. What you cannot buy online is the person who checks the rough-in valve matches the trim, who knows which finish will mark and which won't, and who takes the call when the installer has a question.
Every AXOR bathroom we design is specified as a complete set — brassware, shower, accessories — in one finish, with the installation drawings your fitter needs.

faqs.q: Is AXOR the same as Hansgrohe?
faqs.a: AXOR is Hansgrohe's premium design brand, made in the same factories to the same engineering, with designer collections and the wider finish range.

faqs.q: Can you match an AXOR finish to Gessi or Bette?
faqs.a: Close but rarely identical — brushed finishes vary between houses. We show you the samples side by side in the showroom before you commit.

collections.name: AXOR Citterio and Citterio C
collections.text: Architectural, precise, a long-standing favourite in our developer schemes.

collections.name: AXOR Starck
collections.text: The original 1994 collaboration and its successors.

collections.name: AXOR One and Edge
collections.text: Barber Osgerby's single-control concept; Massaud's cut-metal Edge.

bette.tagline: Baths, shower trays and basins in glazed titanium-steel.
bette.onDisplay: Bette baths and floor-level shower trays on display [confirm models].

knownFor.title: Glazed titanium-steel
knownFor.text: A material that doesn't scratch, stain, flex or fade — and is fully recyclable. Bette guarantees it for 30 years.

knownFor.title: BetteFloor
knownFor.text: The shower tray that made the flush, tiled-look wet room reliable.

knownFor.title: Colour
knownFor.text: Over 400 colours, matt and gloss, including matching basins and trays.

knownFor.title: Freestanding forms
knownFor.text: BetteLux Oval, BetteSilhouette and others — sculptural shapes in a material usually seen built in.

whyZest: A Bette tray or bath is a construction decision as much as a purchase: falls, waste positions, the sub-floor. Our designers detail it with your installer so the wet room drains properly first time.
We have supplied Bette into [X] apartments for developers, so we know the models that survive a decade of tenants and the ones to specify for a family home.

faqs.q: Is steel cold to sit in?
faqs.a: It warms with the water in seconds and holds heat well; the enamel is also noticeably easier to keep clean than acrylic.

faqs.q: Can a Bette tray be fitted flush with the floor?
faqs.a: Yes — BetteFloor is designed for it, with a minimum build-up most floors can take. We detail it with your installer.

collections.name: BetteSilhouette
collections.text: Freestanding steel baths with a seamless skirt.

novello.tagline: Italian bathroom furniture, made to measure.
novello.onDisplay: Novello vanity units and storage on display [confirm].

knownFor.title: Made to measure
knownFor.text: Widths, depths and internal layouts to the centimetre, which is what a real bathroom plan needs.

knownFor.title: Finishes
knownFor.text: Lacquers, veneers, textured laminates and glass fronts, with matching tall units and mirrors.

knownFor.title: Integrated basins
knownFor.text: Ceramic, mineral and stone tops with basins formed in one piece.

whyZest: Furniture is where a bathroom design succeeds or fails on millimetres. Novello is specified from a survey, not a drop-down, and we take responsibility for it fitting.

faqs.a: Made to order in Italy: typically [X] weeks from signed-off design.

villeroy-boch.tagline: Ceramics since 1748, and the sanitaryware most specifiers trust.
villeroy-boch.onDisplay: Villeroy & Boch sanitaryware across the bathroom displays [confirm].

knownFor.title: TitanCeram
knownFor.text: A thinner, harder ceramic that allows the fine edges and flat rims of the current collections.

knownFor.title: Breadth
knownFor.text: From Subway to Antao and Collaro — a range for a student scheme and one for a penthouse, from one supplier.

knownFor.title: CeramicPlus and AntiBac
knownFor.text: Surface treatments that make cleaning easier and are worth having in a family home.

whyZest: We have supplied Villeroy & Boch into [X] apartments for Renaker, Capital & Centric and others — the volume that gives us the programme certainty developers need and the stock knowledge homeowners benefit from.

faqs.q: Which Villeroy & Boch range should I choose?
faqs.a: Depends on the room. Antao and Collaro for a design-led bathroom, Subway 3.0 where budget and durability lead. We'll show you both.

effe.tagline: Italian steam, sauna and spa, built into the home.
effe.onDisplay: Effe steam and spa systems [confirm what is on display].

knownFor.title: Steam at home
knownFor.text: Generators, cabins and shower-steam combinations sized for domestic rooms.

knownFor.title: Design-led
knownFor.text: Collaborations with Marco Williams Fagioli, Talocci Design and others; the Yoku and Aladdin ranges in particular.

knownFor.title: Complete systems
knownFor.text: Sauna, steam and shower in one enclosure where space is tight.

whyZest: Wellness is the part of a bathroom most likely to go wrong without a specialist: ventilation, drainage, power, waterproofing. We design it with the room, not after it, and we have the installer relationships to make it work.

faqs.q: Do I need a wet room for steam?
faqs.a: You need a fully sealed enclosure, which a shower-steam combination provides. A separate steam room needs more depth; we'll tell you honestly what your room can take.

gaggenau.tagline: Appliances built for people who actually cook.
gaggenau.onDisplay: Gaggenau ovens and hobs in the SieMatic displays [confirm].

knownFor.title: The 400 series
knownFor.text: The professional-grade line: combi-steam ovens, Vario cooktops, the 90cm oven.

knownFor.title: Vario cooking
knownFor.text: Modular hobs — induction, teppan, wok, gas — combined to suit how you cook.

knownFor.title: Longevity
knownFor.text: Appliances that are designed to be serviced for decades, not replaced.

whyZest: Appliances are specified into SieMatic cabinetry to the millimetre. We plan the kitchen and the appliance package together so ventilation, power and door clearances are right the first time.

faqs.q: Is Gaggenau worth it over Siemens or Miele?
faqs.a: For most kitchens Siemens or Miele is the right answer and we say so. Gaggenau earns its place when cooking is the point of the room.

oasis.tagline: Italian bathroom furniture with a decorative streak.

knownFor.title: Statement furniture
knownFor.text: Fluted fronts, metal frames, lacquer and marble — furniture that leads the room.

knownFor.title: Made to order
knownFor.text: Sizes and finishes specified per project.

whyZest: Oasis works when it is planned with the brassware, lighting and tiles around it. That is a design appointment, not a shopping basket.

knownFor.title: Glass
knownFor.text: Basins, tops and fronts in coloured and textured glass, made in Tuscany.

knownFor.title: Monolithic basins
knownFor.text: Single-piece glass basins in colours no ceramic matches.

whyZest: Glass needs the right light and the right surroundings. See it in the showroom before you decide; it photographs differently from how it lives.

knownFor.title: Terre di Cielo
knownFor.text: A palette of matt ceramic colours — sixteen and counting — that other makers copy.

knownFor.title: Shapes
knownFor.text: Shui, Era, Le Giare — basins with real sculptural presence.

whyZest: Colour in ceramics has to be matched to tiles, brassware finish and light. We put the samples together in the showroom.

faqs.q: Does coloured ceramic stain or fade?
faqs.a: No — the colour is in the glaze, fired with the piece. It cleans like white ceramic.

knownFor.title: Artisan basins
knownFor.text: Glass, marble and resin basins finished by hand.

whyZest: A Glass Design basin is a piece of furniture. We plan the vanity, the tap and the mirror around it.

sunshower.tagline: Infrared and sunlight in the shower.

knownFor.title: Infrared warmth
knownFor.text: Deep heat while you shower; the wellness case is physiological, not cosmetic.

knownFor.title: Light
knownFor.text: Daylight-spectrum UV in regulated doses, popular with people who miss the sun from October to March.

whyZest: Sunshower needs an electrical spec and the right enclosure; we design it in and brief your electrician.

faqs.a: Dosed and timed by the unit, with the same guidance a dermatologist would give. We'll talk you through it.

victoria-albert.onDisplay: Victoria + Albert baths on display [confirm models].

knownFor.title: Quarrycast
knownFor.text: Volcanic limestone and resin cast in one piece, naturally white, warm to touch and repairable.

knownFor.title: Shape
knownFor.text: Amiata, Barcelona, Ios — forms that work as the centre of a room.

knownFor.title: Colour
knownFor.text: Matt exterior finishes and the Vetralla in jet black, among others.

whyZest: A freestanding bath is a floor-loading, pipework and sightline decision. We plan where it sits, how the tap is fed and how it looks from the door.

faqs.q: How heavy is a Quarrycast bath?
faqs.a: Lighter than cast iron, heavier than acrylic — we check the floor as part of the survey.

siematic.onDisplay: [X] SieMatic displays in Chester: SLX, Pure and Classic [confirm].

knownFor.title: The handleless kitchen
knownFor.text: SieMatic 6006 in 1960 was the first; the SLX, SC and S2 systems are its descendants.

knownFor.title: Style collections
knownFor.text: Pure, Urban, Classic and Mondial — four design languages on one engineering platform.

knownFor.title: Interiors
knownFor.text: Drawer and pull-out systems in oak, aluminium and dark smoked chestnut that make the inside of the kitchen as considered as the front.

knownFor.title: Family-owned
knownFor.text: Third generation, still made in Löhne.

whyZest: SieMatic is sold only through appointed studios, so the question isn't online versus showroom — it's which studio. Ours has designed SieMatic for [X] years, has [X] displays on the floor, and plans the bathroom with the kitchen when a house has both.
The design is the product: layouts, interiors, lighting, appliance integration and worktops, specified in the showroom by someone who will see the project through.

faqs.q: What does a SieMatic kitchen cost?
faqs.a: See our cost guide. Most fall between [£X] and [£X] with appliances and worktops.
Pure is the minimal handleless language; Urban is looser and more lived-in; Classic has framed fronts; Mondial is the luxe end. Most people know within ten minutes in the showroom.
Typically [X] weeks from order; design before that takes as long as it takes to get right.

leicht.tagline: German precision with a wider palette.
leicht.onDisplay: [Confirm whether a Leicht display is on the floor.]

knownFor.title: Colour and material
knownFor.text: Aluro's metal fronts, Les Couleurs Le Corbusier lacquers, real wood and ceramic — a broader palette than most German houses.

knownFor.title: Architectural lines
knownFor.text: Slim worktops, flush panels and frame systems that read as joinery.

whyZest: [Positioning to confirm with Mark: Leicht alongside SieMatic, and when we recommend one over the other.]

collections.name: Aluro
collections.text: Aluminium fronts in oxide bronze and more — see the Chester case study.

hansgrohe.onDisplay: Hansgrohe showers and taps across the displays [confirm].

knownFor.title: Showers
knownFor.text: Raindance, Rainfinity and the iBox universal valve behind most of the showers we fit.

knownFor.title: Reliability
knownFor.text: Parts, service and installer familiarity across the UK.

whyZest: Hansgrohe is widely sold online. What we add is the specification — valve, trim, finish, flow — and the design of the room it sits in.

knownFor.title: Designer collections
knownFor.text: Starck, Cecilie Manz, Sieger Design, Philippe Starck — Duravit was first to put architects' names on ceramics.

knownFor.title: DuraSquare and Happy D.2
knownFor.text: The ranges we specify most.

whyZest: Duravit is specified, not just bought — concealed cisterns, frames, flush plates and furniture all have to agree. We make them agree.
